summary: Tested deployed portfolio desktop and mobile flows. Navigation reaches the Work section visually, case-study modal and experience accordion work, theme control is present, mobile menu closes after selection, and no horizontal overflow was found.

integration_issues.flow: Section heading testability and anchor verification
integration_issues.issue: Rail receives no id prop at its call sites, so every Rail heading renders data-testid="undefined-heading". The Work section is visually reached, but the expected work-heading selector is missing; capabilities and experience heading hooks are likewise unusable.

action_items: Pass explicit section ids (work, capabilities, experience) into Rail or generate stable heading testids so all critical section headings have unique selectors.
critical_code_review_comments: Rail's data-testid is derived from an undefined id because all three Rail usages omit the required id prop; this violates the stated 100% test-id coverage and blocks reliable anchor verification.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Desktop/mobile page loaded. Modal, accordion, mobile menu, and overflow passed. Re-test section heading selectors and all nav anchors after Rail ids are fixed.
rca of the issue: Rail declares an id prop and uses it to build its heading data-testid, but callers render <Rail ...> without id. React therefore produces undefined-heading for all instances. The section wrapper ids still allow visual anchor scrolling, masking the missing critical test hooks.
